# System Overview {#sec-overview}

Cortext turns a stream of signals (text turns, audio chunks, images) into a
SQLite store, and turns a later query into a small, budgeted packet of
evidence. No language model runs on either path. The only learned components
are the frozen AIST-87M multimodal encoder and a 0.1M-parameter
late-interaction reranker over the encoder's per-position features. This
section gives the whole pipeline in one place. The sections after it specify
each stage.

## Write Path

```text
signal (any modality)
  -> AIST embedding (256-d shared space) + per-position features
  -> per-source accumulator: running centroid, drift, coherence, surprisal
  -> online boundary segmentation (Bayesian change-point posterior)
  -> on a boundary: store the closed unit
       memories row (representative embedding e_rep)
       signals rows + object-store payloads (BLAKE3 content ids)
       memory_signal_vectors: one shared-space vector per stored payload
       memory_signal_li_codes: up to 16 int8 late-interaction codes per text or image payload
       memory_text_fts: FTS5 keyword index over long-term text
       standing_signals: lasting directives
       supersedes edges to similar older memories
  -> working-memory admission (bounded slot set)
```

1. **Segmentation decides what a memory is** (@sec-thresholding). Each source
   stream keeps an open unit. A calibrated boundary posterior over surprisal,
   drift, within-unit coherence, topic shift and inter-arrival gaps closes the
   unit at a natural event boundary. A capacity ceiling, a pressure ratio, an
   inactivity boost or an explicit `Flush()` can also close it.
2. **Every closed unit is stored.** The write rule is
   `write_memory = force_write ∨ should_flush`, where `force_write` is set by
   Durable retention. An earlier score threshold
   discarded finished units and cost 7–11% of gold evidence turns
   (@sec-write-pacing). Retention policies choose who closes units: `Natural`
   leaves it to the segmenter, `Durable` closes one per call, `Boundary`
   forces the edge only, and `Ephemeral` stores nothing.
3. **A stored unit is indexed at three granularities.** The unit has one
   pooled vector. Each of its member signals keeps its own shared-space
   vector. Each member payload also keeps late-interaction codes. Its text
   enters the keyword index.

## Read Path

```text
Ephemeral query (any modality; optional reference time T, as_of)
  -> dense unit seeds        (sparse route or exact; family collapse)
  -> member seeds            (best member cosine, max with unit cosine)
  -> keyword seeds           (FTS5 BM25, text queries)
  -> cross-modal seeds       (per-modality z-gated lists)
  -> temporal seeds          (nearest to T, when T is set)
  -> reciprocal-rank fusion  (k = 60)
  -> neighbour deferral
  -> late-interaction MaxSim rerank of the top 64
  -> cut to the output size (11 at neutral knobs)
  -> hydration: contiguity, superseded predecessors, superseding successors,
                standing block, per-blob timestamps
  -> evidence fitting to the caller's byte budget
```

Retrieval (@sec-retrieval) is multi-granularity and hybrid. Dense seeds score
whole units. Member seeds rescue a unit whose pooled vector sits between its
members. BM25 catches rare names and numbers. Cross-modal lists correct for
the modality gap, and the temporal channel answers "around then" queries.
Hydration (@sec-hydration) then rebuilds what a person would recall around
each hit: the adjacent turns, the earlier version of an updated fact, the
newer restatement, and the standing directives. Finally it fits the packet to
the reader's budget.

## Where the Three Knobs Still Act

Focus, Sensitivity and Stability (F, S, T) began as the core of the
architecture. Every rate, threshold and decay was derived from them, and a
homeostatic threshold controller gated persistence. In v5 they are a
macro-control surface over a calibrated default profile. The defaults
(F = S = T = 0.5) are the evaluated operating point. The knobs still change
behavior through closed-form maps:

| Stage | Knob-derived quantities |
|---|---|
| segmentation | boundary hazard, change-point threshold `b_thresh(F,S)`, capacity ceiling `max_signals(F,S,T)`, pressure ratio, inactivity policy |
| composite score | the 12 metric maps and the RLS bootstrap coefficients and forgetting factor (@sec-structural-metrics) |
| working memory | capacity 15–27 slots (21 at neutral), admission weights, chunk budget |
| retrieval breadth | seed count (37 at neutral), seed search breadth (345), output size (11) |
| supersession | similarity band, duplicate threshold, edge cap |
| streaming gate | pacing thresholds and interrupt-gate thresholds (@sec-interrupt) |
| sparse route | capacities $C$, $B$, $A$ (@sec-optimization) |
| maintenance hints | throughput trough fraction and escalation (@sec-consolidation) |

The v5 recall machinery is not knob-derived. Its constants were set by
ablation and hill-climbing on long-horizon evaluations:

* RRF k = 60 and the channel limits;
* the late-interaction depth of 64;
* the contiguity, supersession and standing budgets;
* the 480-byte media charge.

A reader should not expect turning a knob to retune them.

The composite-score stack still runs per signal and still changes packets.
It comprises the emotion projection, 12 metrics and recursive-least-squares
blending. With the RLS blender off, 1,980 of 1,986 LoCoMo retrieved sets
differ (Jaccard 0.29). With the composite score off, all 1,986 differ
(Jaccard 0.08). The score has three consumers, and none of them gates
whether a unit is stored:

* **The stored embedding.** The accumulator centroid at the unit's highest
  score, `e_peak`, is blended into the representative embedding
  (@sec-rep-embedding). It is also the fallback topic anchor for boundary
  detection.
* **Working-memory admission.** The window score `S_window` ranks closed
  units for admission (@sec-wm-gating).
* **Uncertainty.** The recent-score variance is a term of the uncertainty
  estimate, which sets adaptation rates (@sec-math).

The homeostatic threshold controller, the mood integrator and the spike
bypass that once sat on top of this stack were removed. None of them
reached a packet.

## What Was Removed

The 2026-10 leave-one-out ablation (@sec-negative) removed the bio-inspired
lifecycle mechanisms that earlier versions of this paper presented as the
architecture's core:

* multi-timescale strength traces, decay and strength-based eviction;
* reconsolidation drift and retrieval-time reconstruction;
* retrieval-induced forgetting (lateral inhibition);
* clustering consolidation into `ASSOCIATION` centroids, and graph expansion;
* synaptic tagging and capture;
* emotional consolidation and the emotional cascade;
* the NE-like and DA-like neuromodulators, effect scales and the
  encode/retrieve oscillator;
* meta-learned knob priors;
* predictive pre-activation;
* pattern-separation sparse keys and the procedural lane;
* Soft Anchors;
* serial-position effects;
* the focus, sensitivity, stability and influence feedback loops.

A follow-up prune removed what had become unread once every closed unit was
stored. Every removal left packets byte-identical:

* the dynamic threshold controller, its hysteresis and 19 knobs;
* the spike bypass;
* the 6D mood integrator;
* the stored source-reliability metadata and the per-memory context column;
* the dead `affect_retrieval`, `reinforcement_enabled` and
  `sequential_edges_enabled` configuration flags;
* ten always-default `Context::Memory` metric fields.

Each was either inert at the default knobs, leaving packets byte-identical, or
measurably harmful once made to fire. Later sections keep a short record of
each removed mechanism where it used to live, so a reader can see what was
tried. None of them describes current behavior.
